questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula for specific resistance is:
questions.solution:
Specific resistance $\rho$ is given by $\rho = \dfrac{R A}{L}$.

Resistance $R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{W}{q I} = \dfrac{W}{I^2 t}$.

Dimensional formula of work $W = [M L^2 T^{-2}]$.

Dimensional formula of current $I = [A]$ and time $t = [T]$.

Dimensional formula of resistance $R = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-2}]}{[A^2 T]} = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$.

Dimensional formula of area $A = [L^2]$ and length $L = [L]$.

Dimensional formula of specific resistance $\rho = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}] [L^2]}{[L]} = [M L^3 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$.

Answer: $[M\,L^3\,T^{-3}\,A^{-2}]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the equation $X = G^{-1/2}\,h^{1/2}\,c^{5/2}$, where G- universal gravitation constant, h- Planck's constant and c- velocity of light, the dimensions of X are that of
questions.solution:
The dimensional formulas for the given physical quantities are:

$[G] = [M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]$

$[h] = [M L^2 T^{-1}]$

$[c] = [L T^{-1}]$

Given the expression $X = G^{-1/2} h^{1/2} c^{5/2}$, substituting the dimensions:

$[X] = [M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]^{-1/2} [M L^2 T^{-1}]^{1/2} [L T^{-1}]^{5/2}$

$[X] = [M^{1/2} L^{-3/2} T^1] [M^{1/2} L^1 T^{-1/2}] [L^{5/2} T^{-5/2}]$

Combining the powers of $M$, $L$, and $T$:

$[X] = [M^{\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}} L^{-\dfrac{3}{2} + 1 + \dfrac{5}{2}} T^{1 - \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{5}{2}}]$

$[X] = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$

The dimensions $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$ correspond to Energy.

Answer: Energy

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity of a body moving in a viscous medium is given by $v = \dfrac{A}{B+C}   \left[1 - $ e^{$\frac{-t}{B} }\right]$ where t is time; dimensions of A and C are$$
questions.solution:
The exponent of an exponential function must be dimensionless. Therefore, the dimension of $\dfrac{t}{B}$ is $[M^0L^0T^0]$.

$[B] = [t] = [M^0L^0T^1]$

By the principle of homogeneity, quantities added or subtracted must have the same dimensions. Since $B and C$ are added in the denominator, $[C] = [B] = [M^0L^0T^1]$.

The term $\left[1 - e^{\dfrac{-t}{B}}\right]$ is dimensionless. Thus, the dimensions of velocity $v$ must equal the dimensions of $\dfrac{A}{B+C}$.

$[v] = \dfrac{[A]}{[B+C]}$

$[M^0L^1T^{-1}] = \dfrac{[A]}{[M^0L^0T^1]}$

$[A] = [M^0L^1T^{-1}] \times [M^0L^0T^1] = [M^0L^1T^0]$

The dimensions of $A and C$ are $[M^0L^1T^0] and [M^0L^0T^1]$ respectively.

Answer: $[M^0L^1T^0],\ [M^0L^0T^1]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the dimensional formula for electric flux?
questions.solution:
Electric flux $\phi_E$ is defined as the product of electric field $E$ and area $A$, given by $\phi_E = E \cdot A$.

The electric field $E$ is defined as force per unit charge, $E = \dfrac{F}{q}$. The dimensional formula for force $F$ is $[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]$ and for charge $q$ is $[A^1 T^1]$.

Thus, the dimensional formula for electric field $E$ is $\dfrac{[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]}{[A^1 T^1]} = [M^1 L^1 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$.

The dimensional formula for area $A$ is $[L^2]$.

Therefore, the dimensional formula for electric flux $\phi_E$ is $[M^1 L^1 T^{-3} A^{-1}] \times [L^2] = [M^1 L^3 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^1 \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-3} \mathrm{~A}^{-1}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the expression $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{El}^2 \mathrm{ m}^{-5} \mathrmG^{-2}$ where $\mathrm{E}, 1, \mathrm{ m}$ and G represent Energy, Angular Momentum, Mass and Gravitational Constant, the dimensions of P are
questions.solution:
The dimensions of the given physical quantities are as follows:

Energy (E) = $[M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$

Angular Momentum (l) = $[M^1 L^2 T^{-1}]$

Mass (m) = $[M^1]$

Gravitational Constant (G): From $F = G \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, we have $G = \dfrac{F r^2}{m^2} = \dfrac{[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}] [L^2]}{[M^2]} = [M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]$

Now, substitute these dimensions into the expression $P = E l^2 m^{-5} G^{-2}$:

$P = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}] \times ([M^1 L^2 T^{-1}])^2 \times ([M^1])^{-5} \times ([M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}])^{-2}$

$P = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}] \times [M^2 L^4 T^{-2}] \times [M^{-5}] \times [M^2 L^{-6} T^4]$

Combine the powers of M, L, and T:

M: $1 + 2 - 5 + 2 = 0$

L: $2 + 4 + 0 - 6 = 0$

T: $-2 - 2 + 0 + 4 = 0$

Therefore, $P = [M^0 L^0 T^0]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}^0\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $Two physical quantities having the same dimensional formula  \left[\mathrm{M}^1 \mathrm{ L}^{-1} \mathrm{ T}^{-2}\right] are$
questions.solution:
The dimensional formula for Stress is $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Area}} = \dfrac{[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]}{[L^2]} = [M^1 L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

The dimensional formula for Pressure is $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Area}} = \dfrac{[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]}{[L^2]} = [M^1 L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Since both Stress and Pressure have the same dimensional formula $[M^1 L^{-1} T^{-2}]$, they are the correct pair.

Answer: Stress and Pressure

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $R$ and $L$ denote resistance and inductance of a material, then the dimension of $L R$ will be:
questions.solution:
The dimension of resistance $R$ is given by $V = IR$, so $[R] = [V][I]^{-1}$. Since $V = W/q$, $[V] = [M L^2 T^{-2}][A T]^{-1} = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$. Thus, $[R] = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$.

The dimension of inductance $L$ is given by $V = L(dI/dt)$, so $[L] = [V][T][I]^{-1} = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-1}][T][A]^{-1} = [M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}]$.

The dimension of the product $LR$ is $[L][R] = [M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-2}] \times [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}] = [M^2 L^4 T^{-5} A^{-4}]$.

Answer: $M^2 L^4 T^{-5} A^{-4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If units of mass, length and gravitational constant are chosen to fundamental units, the dimensions of time would be
questions.solution:
The dimension of the gravitational constant $G$ is given by the formula $F = G \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, which implies $[G] = \dfrac{[F][r^2]}{[m^2]} = \dfrac{MLT^{-2} L^2}{M^2} = M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}$.

We express time $T$ in terms of mass $M$, length $L$, and gravitational constant $G$ as $T = M^a L^b G^c$.

Substituting the dimensions, we get $[T] = M^a L^b (M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2})^c = M^{a-c} L^{b+3c} T^{-2c}$.

Comparing the powers of $T$ on both sides: $-2c = 1 \Rightarrow c = -1/2$.

Comparing the powers of $M$ on both sides: $a - c = 0 \Rightarrow a = c = -1/2$.

Comparing the powers of $L$ on both sides: $b + 3c = 0 \Rightarrow b = -3c = -3(-1/2) = 3/2$.

Thus, the dimensions of time are $M^{-1/2} L^{3/2} G^{-1/2}$.

Answer: $\mathrmM^{-1 / 2} \mathrm{ L}^{3 / 2} \mathrmG^{-1 / 2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimension $[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{ T}^{-2}]$ is the physical quantity of
questions.solution:
The given dimension is $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Pressure is defined as $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Area}} = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}]}{[L^2]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Energy density is defined as $\dfrac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-2}]}{[L^3]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Since both Pressure and Energy density have the dimension $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$, we evaluate the options provided.

Option (1) Energy density has the dimension $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Option (2) Pressure $\times$ Area is Force, which has dimension $[M L T^{-2}]$.

Option (3) Power $\times$ Time is Energy, which has dimension $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$.

Option (4) $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Pressure}}$ is Area, which has dimension $[L^2]$.

Therefore, Energy density is the correct physical quantity.

Answer: Energy density

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Joule second is the unit of
questions.solution:
The unit of energy is Joule (J) and the unit of time is second (s).

The unit Joule second (J s) corresponds to the product of energy and time.

From the relation $E = h \nu$, where $E$ is energy and $\nu$ is frequency, the unit of Planck constant $h$ is $\dfrac{J}{s^{-1}} = J s$.

Angular momentum $L$ is defined as $L = mvr$. The dimensional formula for angular momentum is $[M L^2 T^{-1}]$.

The dimensional formula for energy is $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$. Multiplying by time $T$, we get $[M L^2 T^{-2}] \times [T] = [M L^2 T^{-1}]$.

Since the dimensions of energy multiplied by time are equivalent to the dimensions of angular momentum, the unit Joule second represents angular momentum.

Answer: Angular momentum

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find the value of '$n$' in the given equation $P=\rho^n v^2$ where '$P$' is the pressure, '$\rho$' density and '$v$' velocity.
questions.solution:
The dimensional formula for pressure $P$ is $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

The dimensional formula for density $\rho$ is $[M L^{-3}]$.

The dimensional formula for velocity $v$ is $[L T^{-1}]$.

Substituting these into the equation $P = \rho^n v^2$, we get:

$[M L^{-1} T^{-2}] = [M L^{-3}]^n [L T^{-1}]^2$

$[M L^{-1} T^{-2}] = [M^n L^{-3n}] [L^2 T^{-2}]$

$[M L^{-1} T^{-2}] = [M^n L^{-3n+2} T^{-2}]$

Comparing the powers of $M$ on both sides, we get $n = 1$.

Checking the powers of $L$: $-1 = -3n + 2 \Rightarrow 3n = 3 \Rightarrow n = 1$.

Checking the powers of $T$: $-2 = -2$, which is consistent.

Answer: $\mathrm{n}=1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the given dimensional formula represents heat capacity
questions.solution:
Heat capacity $C$ is defined as the amount of heat energy $Q$ required to raise the temperature of a substance by an amount $\Delta T$.

The formula is $C = \dfrac{Q}{\Delta T}$.

The dimensional formula for heat energy $Q$ is the same as work or energy, which is $[ML^2T^{-2}]$.

The dimensional formula for temperature change $\Delta T$ is $[K]$.

Substituting these into the formula, we get $C = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[K]} = [ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time dependence of a physical quantity P is give by $\mathrm{P=P}_0 \exp  \left(-\alphat^2\right)$ where \alphais a constant and $ t is time. The constant \alphawill$
options: Have dimensions equal to that of $\mathrm{Pt}^2$
questions.solution:
The given equation is $P = P_0 \exp(-\alpha t^2)$.

In any exponential function of the form $e^x$, the exponent $x$ must be dimensionless. Therefore, the term $\alpha t^2$ must be dimensionless.

$[\alpha t^2] = [M^0 L^0 T^0] = 1$.

Since $t$ represents time, its dimension is $[T]$. Thus, $[\alpha] [T^2] = 1$.

$[\alpha] = [T^{-2}]$.

This implies that the constant $\alpha$ has dimensions of $t^{-2}$.

Answer: Have dimensions of $t^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $R$ and $C$ denote resistance and capacitance of a material, then the dimension of $C R$ will be :
questions.solution:
The dimension of resistance $R$ is given by $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$. Since $V = \dfrac{W}{q}$, we have $R = \dfrac{W}{Iq} = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[A][AT]} = [ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}]$.

The dimension of capacitance $C$ is given by $C = \dfrac{q}{V}$. Since $V = \dfrac{W}{q}$, we have $C = \dfrac{q^2}{W} = \dfrac{[AT]^2}{[ML^2T^{-2}]} = [M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2]$.

The product $CR$ has dimensions $[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2] \times [ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}] = [M^{1-1}L^{2-2}T^{4-3}A^{2-2}] = [M^0L^0T^1]$.

Thus, the dimension of $CR$ is $[T]$, which corresponds to $[M^0L^0T]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following quantity represents the dimensions of momentum?
questions.solution:
The dimension of momentum $p$ is given by $p = mv$, where $m$ is mass (M$) and $v$ is velocity (LT^{-1}$). Thus, the dimensions of momentum are $[MLT^{-1}]$.

Impulse $J$ is defined as the change in momentum, $J = \Delta p = F \Delta t$. The dimensions of force $F$ are $[MLT^{-2}]$ and time $\Delta t$ is $[T]$. Therefore, the dimensions of impulse are $[MLT^{-2}] \times [T] = [MLT^{-1}]$.

Pressure is force per unit area, $[MLT^{-2}] / [L^2] = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$.

Viscosity (coefficient of viscosity) has dimensions $[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$.

Power is work per unit time, $[ML^2T^{-2}] / [T] = [ML^2T^{-3}]$.

Comparing these, impulse has the same dimensions as momentum.

Answer: Impulse

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The physical quantity having the same dimensions as Planck's constant $h$ is
questions.solution:
Dimensional formula of Planck's constant $=\left[\mathrm{M}^{1} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$
Similarly,
Boltzmann constant is given
$$
K=\frac{\text{ Energy }}{\text{ Temperature }}
$$
$\therefore$ The dimension of $K$ is
$$
=\frac{\left[M L^{2} T^{-2}\right]}{[K]}=\left[M^{1} L^{2} T^{-2} K^{-1}\right]
$$
Dimensional formula of force is $\left[\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{l}} \mathrm{L}^{1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$.
Dimensional formula of linear momentum is $\left[M^{1} L^{1} T^{-1}\right]$.
Dimensional formula of angular momentum is $\left[\mathrm{M}^{1} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$.
Hence, angular momentum and Planck's constant have same dimensional formula.

Hence,

\varepsilon=V

&=$\left[$M^{1} L^{2} T^{-3} A^{-1}\right]

L=$\left[\mathrmM^{1} \mathrm{~L}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2} \mathrm{~A}^{-2}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Dimensional formula for the universal gravitational constant $G$ is
questions.solution:
According to Newton's law of gravitation, F=$\frac{G m_{1} m_{2}}{r^{2}}$ where, $F$ = gravitational force between two bodies of masses $m_{1} and m_{2}$,
$r=$ distance between the two masses
and $G=$ universal gravitational constant.
$\therefore \quad G=\frac{F r^{2}}{m_{1} m_{2}} .\therefore \quad[G]=\frac{[F] \left[r^{2}\right]}{ \left[ m_{1}\right]\left[ m_{2}\right]}=\frac{ \left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{L}^{2}\right]}{[ \mathrm{M} ][\m$ mathrm{M}]}=  $\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{ L}^{3} \mathrm{ T}^{-2}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a tunit of Young's modulus?
questions.solution:
Young's modulus, $Y=\frac{\text{ Stress }}{\text{ Strain }}$
Here, strain is a dimensionless quantity and stress is measured in SI unit of $\mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, dyne $\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ or pascal.
So, the Young's modulus has the same unit as stress.
$\therefore \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}  is not a unit of Young's modulus.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The square root of the product of inductance and capacitance has the dimension of
questions.solution:
We know that, in $L-C-R$ series resonant circuit, resonance frequency,
$\begin{aligned} f &=\frac{1}{2 \pi \sqrt{L C}} \\ \Rightarrow \sqrt{L C} &=\frac{1}{2 \pi f} \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \sqrt{L C}=\frac{1}{\omega} \quad[\omega=$ angular frequency $]\begin{aligned}
&\therefore \text{ Dimension$ of $} \sqrt{L C}=\frac{1}{\text{ Dimension of } \omega} \\
&\Rightarrow \quad[\sqrt{L C}]=\frac{1}{[\omega]}=\frac{1}{\left[\mathrm{ T}^{-1}\right]}=[\mathrm{T}]
\end{aligned}$
Hence, square root of the product of inductance $[L]$ and capacitance $[\mathrm{C}]$ has the dimension of time.

questions.solution:
We know that,

Young's modulus, $Y=\frac{\text{ Stress }}{\text{ Strain }}$
$\Rightarrow \quad[Y]=\frac{[\text{ Stress }]}{[\text{ Strain }]}=\frac{[F / A]}{[\text{ Strain }]}$
$=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{M}^{0} \mathrm{~L}^{0} \mathrm{~T}^{0}\right]}$
$=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$
Energy $=$ Work done $=$ Force $\times$ Displacement
$\Rightarrow[$ Energy $]=[$ Force $] \times[$ Displacement $]$
$=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right][\mathrm{L}]=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{2} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$
Hence, we see that dimensions of pressure and Young's modulus is same.

questions.q: If $x=a t+b t^{2}$, where $x$ is measured in metre and $t$ in second, then the dimension of $(b / a)$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $x=a t+b t^{2}$
Here, $x$ is measured in metre $(\mathrm{m})$ and $t$ is in second $(\mathrm{s})$.
So, for dimensional consistency of equation,
Dimensions of $a=[a]=\frac{[x]}{[t]}=\frac{[L]}{[T]}=\left[L^{-1}\right]$
Similarly, for $b,[b]=\frac{[x]}{\left[t^{2}\right]}=\frac{[L]}{\left[\mathrm{T}^{2}\right]}=\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-2}\right]$
$\therefore$ Dimensions of $\left[\frac{b}{a}\right]=\frac{\left[L \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]}{\left[L \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]}=\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]$
